WAFER MAP DEFECT PATTERNS AND THEIR ASSOCIATED PROCESS STEPS

This note summarizes how the spatial signature of a wafer map defect points to
the process step most likely responsible. These associations are used as the
starting point for root cause analysis: the observed pattern narrows down which
process step to suspect first.

Edge-Ring pattern
An Edge-Ring pattern appears as a circular ring located along the wafer's edge.
This pattern is most commonly attributed to problems in the ETCH step. An
Edge-Ring pattern can also arise from thin-film nonuniformity created in the
DEPO step. When an Edge-Ring pattern is observed, the ETCH and DEPO steps should
be investigated first.

Center pattern
A Center pattern, also called a bulls-eye, is concentrated around the wafer
center. A Center pattern typically arises in the DEPO step, where deposition
nonuniformity produces a center-weighted signature. The Center pattern therefore
points to the DEPO step.

Scratch pattern
A Scratch pattern appears as an elongated line of failing dies across the wafer.
A Scratch pattern is frequently associated with the CMP step, where mechanical
abrasion during polishing gouges the wafer surface. A Scratch pattern can also
arise in the CLEAN step, where wafer handling and excessive megasonic energy
damage the surface. When a Scratch pattern is observed, the CMP and CLEAN steps
should be investigated first.

DRY ETCH TROUBLESHOOTING GUIDE

This guide lists common failure modes observed in the ETCH step, their causes,
and the equipment parameter involved in each cause. It is used to drill down
from a suspected process step into specific, checkable causes.

Incorrect etch rate
Incorrect etch rate is a failure mode that occurs in the ETCH step. One cause of
incorrect etch rate is RF power drift, which involves the rf_power parameter.
Another cause of incorrect etch rate is chamber pressure deviation, which
involves the chamber_pressure parameter.

Post-etch residue
Post-etch residue is a failure mode that occurs in the ETCH step. A common cause
of post-etch residue is an excessively high etch rate, which involves the
etch_rate parameter.

Inadequate selectivity
Inadequate selectivity is a failure mode that occurs in the ETCH step. It is
caused by wafer temperature error, which involves the temperature parameter.

DEPOSITION (DEPO) TROUBLESHOOTING GUIDE

This guide lists failure modes observed in the DEPO step, their causes, and the
equipment parameter involved in each cause.

Film thickness nonuniformity
Film thickness nonuniformity is a failure mode that occurs in the DEPO step. One
cause of film thickness nonuniformity is gas flow imbalance, which involves the
gas_flow parameter. Another cause is susceptor temperature drift, which involves
the susceptor_temp parameter.

Low deposition rate
Low deposition rate is a failure mode that occurs in the DEPO step. It is caused
by chamber pressure deviation, which involves the chamber_pressure parameter.

CHEMICAL MECHANICAL PLANARIZATION (CMP) TROUBLESHOOTING GUIDE

This guide lists failure modes observed in the CMP step, their causes, and the
equipment parameter involved in each cause.

Edge over-polish
Edge over-polish is a failure mode that occurs in the CMP step. It is caused by
excessive down force, which involves the down_force parameter.

Slurry maldistribution
Slurry maldistribution is a failure mode that occurs in the CMP step. It is
caused by low slurry flow, which involves the slurry_flow parameter.

Polish induced surface scratching
Polish induced surface scratching is a failure mode that occurs in the CMP step.
One cause of polish induced surface scratching is excessive down force, which
involves the down_force parameter. Another cause is slurry particle
agglomeration, which involves the slurry_flow parameter.

LITHOGRAPHY (LITHO) TROUBLESHOOTING GUIDE

This guide lists failure modes observed in the LITHO step, their causes, and the
equipment parameter involved in each cause.

Critical dimension variation
Critical dimension variation is a failure mode that occurs in the LITHO step. One
cause of critical dimension variation is exposure dose drift, which involves the
exposure_dose parameter. Another cause is defocus of the projection lens, which
involves the focus_offset parameter.

Overlay misregistration
Overlay misregistration is a failure mode that occurs in the LITHO step. It is
caused by stage alignment error, which involves the alignment_offset parameter.

Resist pattern distortion
Resist pattern distortion is a failure mode that occurs in the LITHO step. It is
caused by wafer stage temperature drift, which involves the stage_temp parameter.

WET CLEAN (CLEAN) TROUBLESHOOTING GUIDE

This guide lists failure modes observed in the CLEAN step, their causes, and the
equipment parameter involved in each cause.

Wafer surface scratching
Wafer surface scratching is a failure mode that occurs in the CLEAN step. It is
caused by excessive megasonic power, which involves the megasonic_power
parameter.

Particle residue after clean
Particle residue after clean is a failure mode that occurs in the CLEAN step. One
cause of particle residue after clean is low chemical flow rate, which involves
the flow_rate parameter. Another cause is insufficient rinse time, which involves
the rinse_time parameter.

Chemical attack of the film
Chemical attack of the film is a failure mode that occurs in the CLEAN step. It
is caused by chemical bath temperature drift, which involves the chemical_temp
parameter.

ELECTRICAL DIE SORT (EDS) TROUBLESHOOTING GUIDE

This guide lists failure modes observed in the EDS step, their causes, and the
equipment parameter involved in each cause.

Probe contact failure
Probe contact failure is a failure mode that occurs in the EDS step. It is caused
by probe needle contamination, which involves the contact_resistance parameter.

Wafer chucking instability
Wafer chucking instability is a failure mode that occurs in the EDS step. It is
caused by prober chuck temperature drift, which involves the chuck_temp
parameter.
